title: Audit QA workspace — baseline, gaps, and questions
goal: Audit the QA area to gather a baseline understanding: what exists today, what the area is trying to build, and what is missing/incomplete/needs improvement. Use deep research and sequential thinking; finish with prioritized questions for the owner to answer on how to build or fix each gap. Focus: test strategy, fixtures, end-to-end journeys, regression evidence, and quality gates

in: docs/engineering/agents/qa/ — charter, state, architecture, backlog, interfaces, decisions, verification, working set
The qa default paths declared in WORKING_SET.json
docs/engineering/generated/ — routes, api-routes, components, database-schema, permissions, integrations maps
docs/work-packets/ — existing bounded work packets for this area
.agents/ legacy specialist ledgers that document this area
out: Production code and migration changes (this is a read-only audit)
docs/admin-audit remediation stream unless findings directly affect this domain
Agent registry, task model, and opencode agent definitions

acceptance_criteria: Baseline produced as docs/engineering/agents/qa/BASELINE.md: what the qa area contains today (routes, components, services, API routes, database objects, tests, evidence), each claim backed by a real path reference; plus the area's intended direction, cited to docs/DEVELOPMENT_BACKLOG.md, docs/work-packets/, docs/engineering/agents/qa/BACKLOG.md, and relevant specs.
Started from the domain working set and a packet built via npm run agents:context -- --task QA-001; expanded scope only on evidence, with the path and reason recorded in a checkpoint.

Used deep research and sequential thinking to identify everything that is missing, incomplete, or needs improvement; recorded as docs/engineering/agents/qa/GAPS.md, every item triaged (missing / incomplete / improve) with evidence and location.
